title: Sum of Remoteness of All Cells
summary: Given an n x n matrix grid where each cell has a value or is blocked (-1), calculate the remoteness for each non-blocked cell.
statement: Given an n x n matrix grid where each cell has a value or is blocked (-1), calculate the remoteness for each non-blocked cell. The remoteness of a cell is the sum of values of all non-blocked cells that cannot reach it. Sum these remoteness values for all cells.
constraints: grid is square; each cell is positive or blocked with -1.
Movement connects non-blocked cells sharing a side.
For every non-blocked cell, sum values outside its connected component, then return the total.
hints: Reachability partitions all open cells into connected components.
Find each component’s cell count and value sum, alongside the global value sum.
Every cell in one component has exactly the values outside that component as remote, so multiplying their sum by the component size counts each cell’s remoteness once.
editorial: Every cell in one component has exactly the values outside that component as remote, so multiplying their sum by the component size counts each cell’s remoteness once.

tests.explanation: Four isolated cells see all other values, producing total remoteness thirty-nine.
The top component and isolated bottom cell contribute thirteen in total.
